content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-F000 — Foundation
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `001-foundation` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-11
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-F000 — Foundation: Build the foundation that every later unit uses (project scaffold, design tokens, HTTP client with Either/Failure error mapping, login/sign-up, splash, base navigation, expired-session overlay), as described in docs/input/requirements.md section 12, without implementing RF01–RF10, hardcoding visual values outside design_tokens.dart, or changing the backend."
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Returning user logs in (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A person who already has a Cerne account opens the app, enters their email and password on the login screen, and reaches the main conversation screen (Home/Chat).
16	
17	**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the product — capture, chat, records, settings — is reachable without this. It is the single gate every other unit depends on.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by submitting valid credentials on the login screen and confirming the app lands on Home/Chat; delivers a working, demonstrable access path on its own.
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** a user with a valid existing account and no active session, **When** they enter the correct email and password on the login screen and submit, **Then** they are authenticated and taken to the Home/Chat screen.
24	2. **Given** a user on the login screen, **When** they submit incorrect credentials, **Then** they see a clear, non-crashing error message and remain on the login screen able to retry.
25	3. **Given** a user with no network connection, **When** they submit the login form, **Then** they see a retryable connection-error message rather than the app hanging or crashing.
26	
27	---
28	
29	### User Story 2 - New user creates an account (Priority: P2)
30	
31	A person without a Cerne account switches the same screen to sign-up mode, enters an email and password, and reaches Home/Chat as a newly created user.
32	
33	**Why this priority**: Required for anyone without an account to enter the product at all, but it depends on the same screen and session machinery as login, so it is one step below it.
34	
35	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by toggling to "Criar conta", submitting a new email/password pair, and confirming an account is created and the app lands on Home/Chat.
36	
37	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
38	
39	1. **Given** a person without an account, **When** they switch to "Criar conta" mode, enter a new email and password, and submit, **Then** an account is created and they are taken directly to Home/Chat.
40	2. **Given** a person entering an email that is already registered, **When** they submit the sign-up form, **Then** they see a clear error message and can correct and retry without the app crashing.
41	
42	---
43	
44	### User Story 3 - App launches and routes by session state (Priority: P3)
45	
46	Whenever the app is opened, it shows a brief splash state, checks whether a usable session already exists, and sends the user straight to Home/Chat or to the login/sign-up screen accordingly — without ever leaving them stuck on the splash screen.
47	
48	**Why this priority**: Determines where every single app session begins; it depends on User Story 1 existing but is a thin routing layer on top of it rather than new user-facing capability.
49	
50	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app under three stored-session conditions (valid, expired-but-refreshable, none) and confirming the correct landing screen each time.
51	
52	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
53	
54	1. **Given** a device with a previously stored, still-valid session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands directly on Home/Chat without re-entering credentials.
55	2. **Given** a device with no stored session (first launch, or after logout), **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands on the login/sign-up screen.
56	3. **Given** a device with an expired-but-refreshable session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** the app renews the session in the background and lands on Home/Chat without prompting the user.
57	
58	---
59	
60	### User Story 4 - Navigating between the main screens (Priority: P4)
61	
62	From Home/Chat, the user opens the side menu and moves to Meus Registros or Configurações (today, placeholders), and back, without losing their place.
63	
64	**Why this priority**: Establishes the skeleton every later unit (RF06/RF07/RF05, RF09, etc.) will fill in; it has no functional payload yet, so it ranks below the screens that actually unlock product value.
65	
66	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the side menu from Home/Chat, visiting each destination, and returning, confirming Home/Chat's state is unchanged.
67	
68	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
69	
70	1. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the Meus Registros placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
71	2. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Configurações", **Then** they see the Configurações placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
72	3. **Given** the user is on any main screen, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** the menu overlays the current screen without discarding the state underneath it.
73	
74	---
75	
76	### User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)
77	
78	While the user is actively on a screen (e.g., scrolled partway through Home/Chat), the backend session expires; an overlay appears explaining this and offering to log in again, and once they do, they return to exactly where they were.
79	
80	**Why this priority**: An edge condition of an already-working session (Story 1); important for trust and data safety, but it cannot be exercised until login and at least one screen exist.
81	
82	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirming the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact state.
83	
84	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
85	
86	1. **Given** the user is actively viewing a screen in a particular state (e.g., a given scroll position), **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the current screen without resetting its state.
87	2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible, **When** the user taps "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay is dismissed and the underlying screen is restored exactly as it was.
88	
89	---
90	
91	### Edge Cases
92	
93	- Submitting the login or sign-up form with an empty field shows an inline validation message immediately, with no network call made.
94	- The backend rejects a login or sign-up submission as malformed (non-retryable) — this is shown and handled distinctly from a timeout or offline condition (retryable).
95	- The stored access token is present but its refresh token is itself invalid or expired at launch — the user is routed to the login screen, never left stuck on the splash state.
96	- The session expires a second time while the user is still dismissing a "Sessão expirada" overlay from the first expiration — the overlay persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed with a stale session.
97	- A user opens a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) before its owning unit is built — it renders cleanly as "not yet available" rather than a blank or broken screen.
98	- The app is backgrounded mid-submission of login or sign-up — on resume, the request either completes normally or fails cleanly, and never results in a duplicate account or a duplicate session.
99	
100	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
101	
102	### Functional Requirements
103	
104	- **FR-001**: The project MUST be organized so that every feature added from this unit onward follows one fixed folder convention, so later units have a single place to add their own code without restructuring the foundation.

# Feature Specification: P-F000 — Foundation

**Feature Branch**: `001-foundation` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-11

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-F000 — Foundation: Build the foundation that every later unit uses (project scaffold, design tokens, HTTP client with Either/Failure error mapping, login/sign-up, splash, base navigation, expired-session overlay), as described in docs/input/requirements.md section 12, without implementing RF01–RF10, hardcoding visual values outside design_tokens.dart, or changing the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Returning user logs in (Priority: P1)

A person who already has a Cerne account opens the app, enters their email and password on the login screen, and reaches the main conversation screen (Home/Chat).

**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the product — capture, chat, records, settings — is reachable without this. It is the single gate every other unit depends on.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by submitting valid credentials on the login screen and confirming the app lands on Home/Chat; delivers a working, demonstrable access path on its own.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user with a valid existing account and no active session, **When** they enter the correct email and password on the login screen and submit, **Then** they are authenticated and taken to the Home/Chat screen.
2. **Given** a user on the login screen, **When** they submit incorrect credentials, **Then** they see a clear, non-crashing error message and remain on the login screen able to retry.
3. **Given** a user with no network connection, **When** they submit the login form, **Then** they see a retryable connection-error message rather than the app hanging or crashing.

---

### User Story 2 - New user creates an account (Priority: P2)

A person without a Cerne account switches the same screen to sign-up mode, enters an email and password, and reaches Home/Chat as a newly created user.

**Why this priority**: Required for anyone without an account to enter the product at all, but it depends on the same screen and session machinery as login, so it is one step below it.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by toggling to "Criar conta", submitting a new email/password pair, and confirming an account is created and the app lands on Home/Chat.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a person without an account, **When** they switch to "Criar conta" mode, enter a new email and password, and submit, **Then** an account is created and they are taken directly to Home/Chat.
2. **Given** a person entering an email that is already registered, **When** they submit the sign-up form, **Then** they see a clear error message and can correct and retry without the app crashing.

---

### User Story 3 - App launches and routes by session state (Priority: P3)

Whenever the app is opened, it shows a brief splash state, checks whether a usable session already exists, and sends the user straight to Home/Chat or to the login/sign-up screen accordingly — without ever leaving them stuck on the splash screen.

**Why this priority**: Determines where every single app session begins; it depends on User Story 1 existing but is a thin routing layer on top of it rather than new user-facing capability.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app under three stored-session conditions (valid, expired-but-refreshable, none) and confirming the correct landing screen each time.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a device with a previously stored, still-valid session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands directly on Home/Chat without re-entering credentials.
2. **Given** a device with no stored session (first launch, or after logout), **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands on the login/sign-up screen.
3. **Given** a device with an expired-but-refreshable session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** the app renews the session in the background and lands on Home/Chat without prompting the user.

---

### User Story 4 - Navigating between the main screens (Priority: P4)

From Home/Chat, the user opens the side menu and moves to Meus Registros or Configurações (today, placeholders), and back, without losing their place.

**Why this priority**: Establishes the skeleton every later unit (RF06/RF07/RF05, RF09, etc.) will fill in; it has no functional payload yet, so it ranks below the screens that actually unlock product value.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the side menu from Home/Chat, visiting each destination, and returning, confirming Home/Chat's state is unchanged.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the Meus Registros placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
2. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Configurações", **Then** they see the Configurações placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
3. **Given** the user is on any main screen, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** the menu overlays the current screen without discarding the state underneath it.

---

### User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)

While the user is actively on a screen (e.g., scrolled partway through Home/Chat), the backend session expires; an overlay appears explaining this and offering to log in again, and once they do, they return to exactly where they were.

**Why this priority**: An edge condition of an already-working session (Story 1); important for trust and data safety, but it cannot be exercised until login and at least one screen exist.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirming the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact state.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is actively viewing a screen in a particular state (e.g., a given scroll position), **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the current screen without resetting its state.
2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible, **When** the user taps "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay is dismissed and the underlying screen is restored exactly as it was.

---

### Edge Cases

- Submitting the login or sign-up form with an empty field shows an inline validation message immediately, with no network call made.
- The backend rejects a login or sign-up submission as malformed (non-retryable) — this is shown and handled distinctly from a timeout or offline condition (retryable).
- The stored access token is present but its refresh token is itself invalid or expired at launch — the user is routed to the login screen, never left stuck on the splash state.
- The session expires a second time while the user is still dismissing a "Sessão expirada" overlay from the first expiration — the overlay persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed with a stale session.
- A user opens a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) before its owning unit is built — it renders cleanly as "not yet available" rather than a blank or broken screen.
- The app is backgrounded mid-submission of login or sign-up — on resume, the request either completes normally or fails cleanly, and never results in a duplicate account or a duplicate session.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The project MUST be organized so that every feature added from this unit onward follows one fixed folder convention, so later units have a single place to add their own code without restructuring the foundation.
- **FR-002**: The system MUST define every visual value (color, typography, spacing, corner radius) used anywhere in the app in exactly one central place; no screen delivered by this unit may define a visual value anywhere else.
- **FR-003**: The system MUST provide a single way for any feature to call the backend that always yields either a success result or a typed failure — never an unhandled crash.
- **FR-004**: The system MUST translate every backend error response's error code, message, and retryable flag into a failure the UI can act on, so screens can tell a retryable problem (e.g., timeout) from one that is not (e.g., invalid credentials).
- **FR-005**: The system MUST address the backend using the documented real request path for each operation, not the contract's documentation-only path.
- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to create a new account by submitting an email and password from the sign-up mode of the login screen.
- **FR-007**: Users MUST be able to authenticate with an existing email and password from the login mode of the same screen.
- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to toggle between login and sign-up mode on the same screen without being sent to a different screen.
- **FR-009**: The system MUST check, on every app launch, whether a usable session already exists — renewing it first if it is merely expired-but-renewable — and route the user to Home/Chat when one exists or to the login screen otherwise.
- **FR-010**: The system MUST show a splash state while this session check (and any related background preparation) is in progress, before routing the user anywhere.
- **FR-011**: Users MUST be able to reach Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações from a side menu, and return to Home/Chat from either of them.
- **FR-012**: Meus Registros and Configurações MUST appear as clearly-labeled placeholder screens with no functional behavior from later requirements (RF01–RF10), reserving space for the units that will fill them in.
- **FR-013**: The system MUST show a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of whatever screen the user is on when the backend reports the session has expired, without discarding that screen's state underneath.
- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to dismiss the "Sessão expirada" overlay by re-authenticating, after which the screen underneath MUST be restored to its prior state.
- **FR-015**: The system MUST present a clear, non-crashing message for every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, or session-check can return.
- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any RF01–RF10 requirement; any screen or control belonging to one of them MUST exist only as an inert placeholder, if at all.
- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its contract, or its configuration in any way.

### Key Entities

- **Session**: Represents whether the user is currently authenticated — holds the information needed to stay logged in and to know when it has expired or can be silently renewed. Determines whether a launch routes to Home/Chat or to the login screen, and whether an active screen receives the "Sessão expirada" overlay.
- **Account**: The identity a person signs up with or logs into — an email address and the credential tied to it.
- **Backend Failure**: The error outcome every call introduced by this unit (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can produce — carries enough information to distinguish a retryable problem from a non-retryable one, and to choose the message shown to the user.
- **Placeholder Destination**: A navigable screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) that exists so later units have somewhere to add their functionality, but carries no behavior of its own in this unit.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of returning users with a valid stored session reach Home/Chat automatically after the splash state, with no login step required.
- **SC-002**: A new user can go from the sign-up form to a usable Home/Chat screen in a single successful attempt, with no intermediate screen other than the brief splash state.
- **SC-003**: Every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, and session-check can return produces a readable on-screen message rather than a blank screen, a crash, or an indefinite loading state.
- **SC-004**: A user can reach each of the main screens (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) from the side menu, and return to Home/Chat, in 2 taps or fewer, every time.
- **SC-005**: When a session expires while a screen is in a particular state, that same state (e.g., scroll position, visible content) is unchanged after the user re-authenticates, in every observed case.
- **SC-006**: Every screen delivered by this unit visually matches the prototype's documented colors, typography, and spacing, with zero visual values defined outside the single central source.

## Assumptions

- Biometric/PIN authentication (RF03) is its own delivery unit, built immediately after this one. Until it exists, the splash state routes directly between itself and the login/sign-up screen — the biometric step shown in the prototype's navigation map is intentionally skipped for this unit and will be inserted by the RF03 unit.
- Re-authenticating from the "Sessão expirada" overlay goes to the login screen (not to a biometric step), for the same reason — RF03 is not yet part of the app.
- Sign-up collects only an email and a password, matching both the prototype (which shows no additional fields) and the backend's sign-up contract.
- Session renewal is attempted silently in the background whenever a request fails because the session has merely expired; the "Sessão expirada" overlay is shown only once silent renewal itself is not possible.
- Where this unit's side menu is shown, "Planos de Ação" may exist as an inert placeholder entry per the product's extension-feature policy, but is not required navigation for this unit — only Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações are.
- Access and refresh tokens are kept on the device between app launches so a returning user is not asked to log in every time; the specific on-device storage mechanism is an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification.
- Every error this unit's calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes; no other error shape is expected from these calls.

# Implementation Plan: P-F000 — Foundation

**Branch**: `001-foundation` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; see spec header)

**Date**: 2026-10-11 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-foundation/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md` §12
(delivery order) and §13 (technical constraints), and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`.

## Summary

F000 is the foundation every later unit (RF03 → RF09) builds on: the Flutter project scaffold and
Clean Architecture folder convention, `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` as the single visual-value
source, a `dio`-based HTTP client whose repositories return `Either<Failure, T>` (fpdart) mapped
from the backend's closed 13-code error taxonomy, the login/sign-up screen (toggle, not two
screens), splash-time session check with silent refresh, base navigation (Home/Chat shell, side
menu/drawer, Meus Registros and Configurações placeholders), and the "Sessão expirada" overlay that
preserves underlying screen state. It consumes exactly 4 of the backend's 23 Edge Functions
(`auth-signup`, `auth-login`, `auth-refresh`, `auth-session`) and implements no RF01–RF10 behavior.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable channel), pinned to the project via
`fvm` (already present on this machine's global fvm cache — see [research.md](./research.md) R1).

**Primary Dependencies**:
- `flutter_bloc` (state management — fixed by constitution)
- `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>` — fixed by constitution)
- `dio` (HTTP client — chosen, see R2)
- `go_router` (navigation — chosen, see R3)
- `get_it` (service locator / DI — chosen, see R4)
- `flutter_secure_storage` (on-device token persistence — chosen, see R5)
- `equatable` (value equality for states/entities/failures)
- Dev-only: `mocktail` (fixed by constitution), `bloc_test`

**Storage**: `flutter_secure_storage` only — persists `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`
between launches (per spec Assumptions). No local database/cache is introduced by F000.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` for bloc/presentation logic, `mocktail` for every test
double (data sources, repositories), coverage measured with `fvm flutter test --coverage` and a
`lib/**/domain/**`-scoped lcov filter for the RNF07 gate (≥80%).

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait orientation only (constitution + requirements §13). No
product-specified minimum iOS deployment target exists in the inputs; the pinned Flutter SDK's
`flutter create` default is kept as-is (see R8) rather than inventing a floor.

**Project Type**: Single Flutter mobile app consuming a frozen, already-documented backend over
HTTPS Edge Functions. No backend/server code is part of this repository.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 — local actions reflected in the UI in <100 ms; any network call
exceeding 300 ms shows a loading indicator (skeleton/spinner, per prototype's `Skeleton` component).

**Constraints**:
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers (`data/`, `domain/`, `presentation/`) per feature (Principle V).
- Every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (Principle II, RNF09).
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV, RNF08).
- Domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor any `data/` class (Principle V, RNF06).
- No change to the backend, its contract, or its configuration (Principle III, FR-017).
- No direct AI-provider calls from the app (Principle III).
- Real request paths only — `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>`, never the OpenAPI REST path
  (Principle III, FR-005).
- `.env` carries exactly `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, never committed.
- No RF01–RF10 functional behavior; any such control exists only as an inert placeholder (FR-016).

**Scale/Scope**: 5 screens (Splash, Login/Sign-up toggle, Home/Chat shell, Meus Registros
placeholder, Configurações placeholder) + 1 modal overlay (Sessão expirada) + 1 navigation drawer;
consumes 4 of the backend's 23 operations; 0 persisted business data of its own (tokens only).

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this
section.*

| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only; all open decisions resolved in research.md rather than left blocking. |
| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart` `Either`, `mocktail` adopted as-is. `whisper_ggml` is out of scope for F000 (no audio capture exists yet) — not a violation, simply not yet introduced. |
| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only `auth-signup`/`auth-login`/`auth-refresh`/`auth-session` called, via `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>`; `apikey` header on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` for signup/login/refresh, `Bearer <access token>` for `auth-session`. `.env` already gitignored, untouched by this plan. |
| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | `design_tokens.dart` is a Phase 1 output; see data-model.md and R9. |
| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | See Project Structure below; domain layer kept Flutter- and data-free. |
| RNF01 (latency) | PASS | Loading indicator required >300 ms on the 4 auth calls and the splash session check. |
| RNF02/03/04 (PII, retention, RLS) | N/A to F000 | Backend-side; no app logic introduced or required. |
| RNF05 (hard delete) | N/A to F000 | Belongs to the Settings/RF09 unit; Configurações is an inert placeholder here. |
| RNF06 (layer violations) | PASS | Enforced structurally by folder convention; domain entities/usecases/repositories contain no Flutter or data imports. |
| RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | Applies to `session` and `auth` domain layers delivered here. |
| RNF08 (visual fidelity) | PASS | All 5 screens sourced from `design_tokens.dart`; see data-model.md. |
| RNF09 (Either + 15/15 error scenarios) | PARTIAL BY DESIGN, not a violation | RNF09's full target is 5 write endpoints × 3 failures, reached incrementally across the whole delivery order (requirements.md §12). F000 contributes the `Either` pattern itself (used by every later repository) plus full timeout/malformed/offline coverage for its own 3 write-ish auth calls (signup, login, refresh — `auth-session` is a read). No Complexity Tracking entry needed: this is the staged rollout the delivery order already anticipates, not a deviation. |

*Post-Phase-1 re-check: see "Post-Design Constitution Check" at the end of this document.*

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/001-foundation/
├── plan.md              # This file
├── research.md          # Phase 0 output
├── data-model.md        # Phase 1 output
├── quickstart.md        # Phase 1 output
├── contracts/           # Phase 1 output
│   ├── http-client.md
│   ├── failure-taxonomy.md
│   ├── auth-repository.md
│   └── session-repository.md
└── tasks.md             # Phase 2 output (/speckit-tasks — not created here)
```

### Source Code (repository root)

No Flutter project exists yet in this repository (no `pubspec.yaml`/`lib/` found) — F000 creates it.

```text
cerne-ciclo-a/                      # repo root (unchanged: docs/, .specify/, specs/, .env)
├── .fvmrc                          # pins Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4
├── pubspec.yaml
├── lib/
│   ├── main.dart
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── design_tokens.dart          # single source of colors, typography, spacing, radii
│   │   ├── network/
│   │   │   ├── api_client.dart         # dio wrapper: base URL + apikey + bearer injection
│   │   │   ├── failure.dart            # sealed Failure hierarchy, all 13 error codes
│   │   │   └── error_mapper.dart       # {code,message,retryable,requestId} -> Failure
│   │   ├── storage/
│   │   │   └── secure_token_storage.dart
│   │   ├── routing/
│   │   │   ├── app_router.dart         # go_router config + root navigatorKey
│   │   │   └── app_routes.dart

│   └── features/

│       ├── session/

│       │   │   └── session_repository_impl.dart
│       │   ├── domain/

│       │   │   ├── repositories/session_repository.dart
│       │   │   └── usecases/check_session_usecase.dart
│       │   └── presentation/
│       │       ├── bloc/session_bloc.dart            # splash routing + expired-session trigger
│       │       └── widgets/session_expired_overlay.dart
│       ├── auth/
```

**Structure Decision**: Single Flutter mobile app at the repo root (`lib/`, `test/`), following the
constitution's fixed `core/` + `features/<feature>/{data,domain,presentation}` convention exactly.
`docs/`, `.specify/`, and `specs/` are untouched. No `backend/`/`api/` tree is created — the backend
is frozen and consumed only through `docs/input/backend/`.

## Complexity Tracking

## Post-Design Constitution Check

441	## Dependencies & Execution Order
442	
443	### Phase Dependencies
444	
445	- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
446	- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup — BLOCKS all user stories.
447	- **User Stories (Phase 3–7)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
448	  - US1 (P1) has no dependency on another story.
449	  - US2 (P2) extends US1's `auth_remote_data_source.dart`/`auth_repository_impl.dart`/`auth_bloc.dart`/
450	    `login_signup_page.dart` in place — do US1 first.
451	  - US3 (P3) is independent of US1/US2's files but its splash routes to the Home/Chat page US1
452	    creates (T028) — do US1 first for a meaningful manual test, though US3's own tasks touch no
453	    US1/US2 files.
454	  - US4 (P4) extends US1's `home_chat_shell_page.dart` (T028) — do US1 first.
455	  - US5 (P5) extends US3's `session_bloc.dart` (T047) and needs US1/US2's login screen as the
456	    re-authentication destination — do US1 and US3 first.
457	- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all five user stories being complete.
458	
459	### Within Each User Story
460	
461	- Tests are written first and MUST fail before their matching implementation task.
462	- Domain entities/interfaces before use cases; use cases before blocs; blocs before pages.
463	- Data-layer classes (`*_remote_data_source.dart`, `*_repository_impl.dart`) before the
464	  `service_locator.dart` registration task that wires them in.
465	
466	### Parallel Opportunities
467	
468	- All Setup tasks marked [P] (T003, T004) can run in parallel once T001/T002 finish.
469	- Within Foundational, T005, T007, T009, T011 (and the chain T012→T013) can run in parallel; T006,
470	  T008, T010 each wait only on their own listed dependency.
471	- Within each story's test block, tasks against distinct new files are marked [P]; tasks that extend
472	  a file an earlier story's task already created (e.g. T031/T032/T033, T034/T035/T037/T038) are not
473	  marked [P] and run after that earlier task.

# Tasks: P-F000 — Foundation

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-foundation/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (http-client.md,
failure-taxonomy.md, auth-repository.md, session-repository.md), quickstart.md — all present.

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) as
"PASS (gate carried into tasks)" and RNF09 requires 15/15 write-endpoint failure scenarios covered
by `mocktail`; `quickstart.md`'s Automated checks run `flutter test --coverage` against a
`lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter. Domain-layer unit tests (`mocktail`) and bloc tests (`bloc_test`)
are therefore generated per story; User Story 4 (pure navigation/presentation, no domain code) has
none, matching the domain-only scope of the gate.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (P1–P5 from spec.md) to enable independent
implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1–US5, mapping to spec.md's five user stories
- Exact file paths are given per plan.md's Project Structure

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter app at the repo root: `lib/`, `test/` (plan.md Project Structure; no
`backend/`/`api/` tree — the backend is frozen and consumed only through `docs/input/backend/`).

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Create the Flutter project itself; nothing in `lib/` exists yet in this repo.

- [X] T001 Run `fvm install 3.47.5` (if not already the cached default) and `fvm use 3.47.5` at the
  repo root, writing `.fvmrc`; then `fvm flutter create .` to scaffold the Flutter project in place
  (iOS platform only — remove/ignore the android/, web/, etc. platform folders `flutter create`
  generates, per plan.md Target Platform: "iOS, portrait orientation only") (research.md R1)
- [X] T002 Add to `pubspec.yaml` dependencies: `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `dio`, `go_router`,
  `get_it`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `equatable`, `flutter_dotenv` (the last is this task's own
  reasonable choice for loading the repo-root `.env`'s `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`,
  per Constitution Principle I — the stack list leaves env loading unfixed); dev dependencies:
  `mocktail`, `bloc_test` (plan.md Technical Context, Constitution Principle II)
- [X] T003 [P] Configure `analysis_options.yaml` with the standard Flutter lint set plus
  `avoid_relative_lib_imports`/import-ordering rules that make a `package:flutter` or `data/` import
  inside any `domain/` folder a visible lint failure (supports RNF06's "0 layer violations" gate,
  checked at Polish phase by `flutter analyze`)
- [X] T004 [P] Obtain and vendor the Fraunces, Karla, and IBM Plex Mono font files under
  `assets/fonts/`, and declare them under `flutter: fonts:` in `pubspec.yaml` with the weights used
  by `design_tokens.dart` (600 for Fraunces, 400/500/700 for Karla, 500 for IBM Plex Mono) — bundled
  as local assets, not `google_fonts`, per research.md R9

**Checkpoint**: `fvm flutter pub get` succeeds; project scaffold exists.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The design-token source, the `Either<Failure, T>` network stack, secure storage,
routing skeleton, and DI wiring that every user story below depends on.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [X] T005 [P] Create `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`: 14 panel colors (`colorPrimary #1F3D34`,
  `colorPrimaryPressed #16281F`, `colorOnPrimary #F5F1E8`, `colorAccent #C98A3E`,
  `colorOnAccent #241C0D`, `colorSecondary #7C8B6F`, `colorSurfaceBg #F2EFE7`,
  `colorSurfaceElevated #FBF9F4`, `colorBorder #E1DACB`, `colorTextPrimary #241F19`,
  `colorTextSecondary #6B6255`, `colorError #B3402A`, `colorSuccess #4C6B4F`,
  `colorWarningSync #C98A3E`, `colorInfoOffline #5C7A93`) plus `colorChatBubbleUser #D9DFD3` (used
  by this unit's Home/Chat shell); 8 `TextStyle` constants exactly as prototype-extract.md §3 states
  (`textDisplayLg` Fraunces 600·32/38, `textHeadlineMd` Fraunces 600·24/30, `textTitleLg` Karla
  700·20/26, `textTitleSm` Karla 700·16/22, `textBodyLg` Karla 400·16/24, `textBodyMd` Karla
  400·14/20, `textLabelMd` Karla 500·13/18, `textMonoCaption` IBM Plex Mono 500·12/16·letter-spacing
  0.2); spacing (`spacingXs` 4, `spacingSm` 8, `spacingMd` 16, `spacingLg` 24, `spacingXl` 32,

  999, all `double` dp); `elevation1`/`elevation2` as `BoxShadow`/`List<BoxShadow>` matching

  Design Tokens, RNF08/Principle IV: zero visual values hardcoded anywhere else)
- [X] T006 [P] Create `lib/core/theme.dart` building a single `ThemeData` solely from

- [X] T007 [P] Create `lib/core/network/failure.dart`: `sealed class Failure extends Equatable` with
  `message`/`requestId` fields and the 13 closed-taxonomy subtypes, each with its fixed `code` and
  `retryable` pair exactly per contracts/failure-taxonomy.md (`AuthExpiredFailure`/`AUTH_EXPIRED`/
  false, `AuthInvalidFailure`/`AUTH_INVALID`/false, `NetworkTimeoutFailure`/`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`/true,
  `NetworkOfflineFailure`/`NETWORK_OFFLINE`/true, `ValidationFailure`/`VALIDATION_ERROR`/false,
  `PiiCheckFailedFailure`/`PII_CHECK_FAILED`/true, `EmbeddingFailedFailure`/`EMBEDDING_FAILED`/true,
  `AiGenerationTimeoutFailure`/`AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`/true, `NotFoundFailure`/`NOT_FOUND`/false,
  `RateLimitedFailure`/`RATE_LIMITED`/true, `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure`/`EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`/false,
  `PayloadTooLargeFailure`/`PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`/false, `OcrNoTextFailure`/`OCR_NO_TEXT`/false); no
  `package:flutter` import (RNF06 — this file lives in the domain boundary)
- [X] T008 Create `lib/core/network/error_mapper.dart` with
  `ErrorMapper.fromResponse(Map<String, dynamic> body)` performing the exhaustive `code` → `Failure`
  subtype switch; an unrecognized `code` MUST NOT throw — map it to a defensive `ValidationFailure`
  instead (contracts/failure-taxonomy.md; FR-003 "never an unhandled crash") (depends on T007)
- [X] T009 [P] Create `lib/core/storage/secure_token_storage.dart` wrapping
  `flutter_secure_storage` with read/write/delete for `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`
  (int, unix seconds), `tokenType` — iOS Keychain-backed, never plaintext (data-model.md Session;
  research.md R5)
- [X] T010 Create `lib/core/network/api_client.dart`'s `ApiClient` class and `AuthMode` enum exactly
  per contracts/http-client.md: `call(String function, {required String method, body, pathSegments,
  authMode = AuthMode.userSession})`; URL = `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>/<pathSegments...>` read
  from `.env` via `flutter_dotenv` (never the OpenAPI REST-notation path — Principle III, FR-005);
  every call carries `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`; `Authorization` is `Bearer <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`
  for `AuthMode.anonKey` or `Bearer <stored accessToken>` (from `SecureTokenStorage`) for

  discarded); non-2xx with `{code,message,retryable,requestId}` body → `ErrorMapper.fromResponse(...)`
  → `Left(Failure)`; a dio connection-error/no-response condition → `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure(...))`

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

## Scope & Delivery Boundaries

- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.

# Contract: `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`)

The single way any feature calls the backend (FR-003). Every later unit's `data/` layer depends on
this, never on `dio` directly.

## Construction

```dart
class ApiClient {
  ApiClient({required Dio dio, required SecureTokenStorage tokenStorage, required String anonKey});

  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
    String function, {               // e.g. "auth-login" — never a REST path (FR-005)
    required String method,          // "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "DELETE"
    Map<String, dynamic>? body,
    List<String>? pathSegments,      // appended in the order the OpenAPI path declares them
    AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession, // or AuthMode.anonKey
  });
}

enum AuthMode { anonKey, userSession }
```

## Behavior

1. **URL construction**: `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>/<pathSegments...>` — read from `.env`'s
   `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`. Never the OpenAPI document's REST-notation path (Principle III, FR-005).
2. **Headers, every call**: `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>` (from `.env`).
3. **`Authorization` header**:
   - `AuthMode.anonKey` → `Bearer <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>` — used for `auth-signup`, `auth-login`,
     `auth-refresh` (no user session exists yet or is being replaced).
   - `AuthMode.userSession` → `Bearer <stored accessToken>` (read from `SecureTokenStorage`) — used
     for `auth-session` and every `bearerAuth` operation added by later units.
4. **Success**: returns `Right(data)` where `data` is the parsed `data` object from the response
   envelope (`{data, meta}`), discarding `meta` unless a future unit's contract says otherwise.
5. **Failure**: any non-2xx response with the `{code, message, retryable, requestId}` error body is
   passed to `ErrorMapper.fromResponse(...)` → `Left(Failure)` (see `failure-taxonomy.md`). A dio
   `DioExceptionType.connectionError`/no-response condition is mapped directly to
   `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure(...))` without a parse attempt (error-taxonomy.md: `NETWORK_OFFLINE`
   never arrives as an HTTP response). A dio timeout is mapped to `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure(...))`.
6. **Never throws** past this boundary — every exception dio can raise is caught and mapped to a
   `Failure` before returning, satisfying FR-003 ("never an unhandled crash").

## Who depends on this

`AuthRemoteDataSource`, `SessionRemoteDataSource` (this unit) and every later unit's `*RemoteDataSource`.

# Quickstart: validating P-F000 — Foundation

Prerequisites, run commands, and expected outcomes for proving this unit's 5 user stories end to
end. Interface details (headers, URLs, failure types) are in `contracts/`; entity/state details
are in `data-model.md`.

## Prerequisites

- `fvm use 3.47.5` run once at the repo root (installs/links the pinned SDK — see research.md R1).
- `.env` present at the repo root with `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (already exists
  in this repo; never commit it).
- `fvm flutter pub get`.
- A real or simulated iOS device/runner (`fvm flutter devices`), since the target platform is iOS.

## Setup

```bash
fvm flutter pub get
fvm flutter run -d <ios-device-or-simulator-id>
```

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                   # 0 issues, incl. no flutter imports under domain/ (RNF06)
fvm flutter test --coverage                            # unit + bloc tests (mocktail, bloc_test)
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/*/domain/*' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain_html    # inspect: >= 80% (RNF07)
```

## Manual / integration validation scenarios

Each maps directly to a spec.md Acceptance Scenario.

1. **Login (User Story 1)**
   - Launch with no stored session → login screen.
   - Enter a valid, existing email/password → lands on Home/Chat.
   - Enter a wrong password → inline, non-crashing error, stays on login screen, can retry.
   - Turn off network, submit → retryable connection-error message, no hang/crash.

2. **Sign-up (User Story 2)**
   - From the login screen, tap the toggle link → title/CTA switch to "Criar conta" (same screen,
     no navigation).
   - Submit a brand-new email/password → account created, lands directly on Home/Chat.
   - Submit an already-registered email → clear error, form stays editable, no crash.

3. **Launch routing (User Story 3)** — exercise all three stored-session conditions:
   - Valid session on device → splash, then straight to Home/Chat, no credentials re-entered.
   - No stored session (fresh install, or after a manual token wipe) → splash, then login screen.
   - Expired-but-refreshable session (manually expire the stored `accessToken`, keep a valid
     `refreshToken`) → splash, silent `auth-refresh`, lands on Home/Chat without any prompt.

4. **Base navigation (User Story 4)** — confirms SC-004 (≤2 taps each way)
   - From Home/Chat, tap ☰ (1 tap) → drawer opens, see Meus Registros, Configurações.
   - Tap Meus Registros (2 taps total) → visible; tap ☰ then Home/Chat (≤2 taps) to return →
     chat shell state (e.g., scroll position) unchanged.
   - Repeat for Configurações, confirming ≤2 taps each direction.
   - Opening the drawer itself visibly scrims the current screen without resetting it.

5. **Session-expired overlay (User Story 5)**
   - Get to a known state on a screen (e.g., scroll Home/Chat partway).
   - Force a session-expired response (e.g., revoke/expire the access token server-side, or stub it
     in a debug build) while that screen is active.
   - Confirm the "Sessão expirada" card appears over a light scrim, screen content still visible
     and unchanged underneath.
   - Tap "Entrar novamente", re-authenticate → overlay dismissed, screen state (scroll position)
     restored exactly.
   - Repeat the forced expiry while the overlay is still visible (before dismissing) → overlay
     persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed.

## Expected outcome

All 5 scenarios above pass; `flutter analyze` and `flutter test --coverage` are clean; the
`lib/**/domain/**` coverage report meets RNF07; no screen's rendered output uses a color, font, or
spacing value traceable to anything other than `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (spot-check via code
review, since this is not yet an automated lint in this unit).

  description: '**How to build the real URL:** there is no router — each operation is served by its own Edge Function,

    `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path parameters, in the same order as they appear in the `path`, as
    final segments>` — any literal segment of the `path` after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `/chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry`)

# Error taxonomy — 13 codes

Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.

| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |

**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.

**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.
